title: Food chains, webs and energy pyramids

match.reason: No single bank point teaches the whole new point: the food chain and web card lacks energy pyramids and decomposers, the energy flow card covers energy loss per level but not food chains or decomposers, and the producers and decomposers card lacks energy transfer.

draft.title: Food chains, webs and energy pyramids
card: A food chain shows how energy passes from one living thing to the next. It starts with a producer, such as grass, which makes its own food using sunlight. Consumers get energy by eating other living things.
A food web joins many food chains together. Most animals eat more than one kind of food, so a web shows these links better than a single chain.
Only a small part of the energy at one level passes to the next. The rest is used for living or lost as heat. So an energy pyramid is widest at the producers and narrows towards the top.
Decomposers, such as fungi and bacteria, break down dead plants and animals. They return matter to the soil, where plants can use it again.
draft.remember: Energy passes along food chains, with only a small part reaching each next level. Decomposers return matter to the soil.

a.q: A pyramid shows 10 000 units of energy in grass but far less in the hawks at the top. What explains this?
opts: Most energy at each level is used or lost as heat
Hawks need less food than any animal below them
Grass passes all of its energy to the next level
Decomposers take energy from the top level first
a.why: Most energy at each level is used for living or lost as heat, so only a small part passes up to the next level. Grass does not pass on all of its energy, because much of it is used by the grass itself.
a.clue: Think about what happens to the energy at each level.

b.q: In a paddock near Orange, grass is eaten by grasshoppers, which are eaten by lizards, which are eaten by hawks. A farmer finds that a dead lizard has broken down and the soil beneath it is richer. Which living things most directly caused this?
opts: Fungi and bacteria acting as decomposers
b.why: Decomposers break down dead animals and return matter to the soil. Grass is a producer and makes food from sunlight, but it does not break down dead animals.
b.clue: Which group breaks down dead things?

wants.brief: An energy pyramid with four levels. From the bottom: producers, primary consumers, secondary consumers, tertiary consumers. Each level is narrower than the one below it, with the producers widest.
wants.why: It shows how the pyramid narrows towards the top.

a.best: Most energy at each level is used or lost as heat

b.best: Fungi and bacteria acting as decomposers
